title: Mitigating and Emphatic Denial: aligha, korántsem, éppenséggel

sections.title: Nuances of Epistemic Doubt with 'aligha'
sections.content: While everyday Hungarian uses 'nem valószínű' (not likely), B2 discourse prefers 'aligha' (hardly / scarcely) to express nuanced skepticism. 'Aligha' precedes the verb or focused element and softens categorical negation into an educated doubt: 'Ez aligha valósul meg' (This will hardly be realized). Never combine 'aligha' with 'nem' (*aligha nem is ungrammatical double negative in modern Hungarian).

sections.title: Emphatic Refutation: 'korántsem', 'cseppet sem', and Concession with 'éppenséggel'
sections.content: 'Korántsem' (by no means / far from it) directly challenges an unfounded presupposition: 'A feladat korántsem egyszerű' (The task is far from simple). 'Cseppet sem' (not in the least / not a bit) emphasizes zero degree of impact: 'Cseppet sem zavar' (It doesn't bother me in the least). In contrast, 'éppenséggel' indicates an unexpected possibility or polite concession: 'Éppenséggel megpróbálhatjuk' (We could actually try it / it's not out of the question).

sections.title: Denial and Mitigation Particles at B2
rows: by no means / far from (refuting assumption)
not in the least (emphatic zero degree)
as a matter of fact / actually (concessive possibility)

items.spanish: Az új javaslat aligha oldja meg a fennálló gazdasági nehézségeket.
items.english: The new proposal will hardly solve the existing economic difficulties.

items.spanish: A helyzet korántsem olyan kétségbeejtő, mint amilyennek a hírek láttatják.
items.english: The situation is by no means as desperate as the news makes it seem.

items.spanish: A vendég viselkedése cseppet sem zavarta az idős házigazdát.
items.english: The guest's behavior did not disturb the elderly host in the least.

items.spanish: Éppenséggel maradhatnánk még egy órát, ha nem sietsz a vonathoz.
items.english: As a matter of fact, we could stay another hour if you're not rushing to the train.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Use 'aligha' before verbs without 'nem' to sound natural and elegant: say 'Aligha hiszem' instead of 'Nem hiszem nagyon'.
